volumes.authoring.code.contract: Code authoring contract: use %s and current dictionary %s. Under the official starter dictionary only, G means genuinely cross-domain and Z means sufficient evidence was understood but no named category fits; insufficient evidence is not Z and must be reported. Classification or dictionary gaps never enter S. Under the official starter dictionary, a test file may use A=T, but B normally remains the tested functional domain; use B=Q only for test or quality infrastructure itself. Custom formal Meta meanings remain authoritative. FRAS v2 limits are F<=%d runes, R<=%d runes/%d items, A<=%d runes/%d items. S admits only non-inferable, error-preventing facts and uses %s. For C6-C9 objects, actively look for evidence-backed S constraints. Use S only when the constraint cannot be inferred from F/R/A and affects system understanding or modification. Keep S:- when no qualifying constraint exists. R accepts exact managed identities such as %s or %s, separates multiple identities with %q, and uses %q for no strong relation. Dotted tags and bare relation names are read compatibility only and must not be authored. The example calibrates field separation only; do not copy its semantics.

volumes.authoring.meta: Read authoring_meta before authoring any affected Volume candidate. It is the exact formal aoci.meta.txt bytes returned by aoci_header; runtime instructions complete compatibility contracts without changing or substituting those bytes.
volumes.authoring.transport: Author every candidate directly as aoci_update_entry arguments: this batch is sized to be written inline in one call, so no intermediate files, helper scripts, or shell staging are needed, and none of the candidate facts have to be copied anywhere. R and S are bounded by token bands as well as rune quotas: a token is UTF-8 bytes/3, so one CJK character is one token and the per-C ceilings in governance.budget (r and s) bind before the rune quotas for CJK text. If the context is lost mid-batch, call aoci_maintain again: the unchanged repository reproduces the same batch and candidate identities.
